speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the nature of your cough, and do you have any fever or chest pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Chest X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 9,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 14.0 g/dL, Platelets 230,000 /μL; Chest X-Ray: Bilateral interstitial infiltrates suggestive of pulmonary fibrosis. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any worsening of your breathlessness with exertion? REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary Function Tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pulmonary Function Tests: Reduced FVC and FEV1 with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, indicating a restrictive pattern.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you ever been exposed to asbestos, silica, or other industrial dusts, and do you have a history of autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis or scleroderma? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Panel (ANA, RF, CCP).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; since your autoimmune panel is normal, we can likely rule out connective tissue diseases. Have you noticed any dry eyes or dry mouth, and do you have a history of kidney stones or gallstones? REQUEST TEST: Schirmer's Test, Anti-Ro/La Antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the normal Schirmer's test and negative Anti-Ro/La antibodies make Sjögren's syndrome unlikely. Given the restrictive lung pattern and interstitial infiltrates, have you noticed any skin changes like tightening or thickening of your fingers, or difficulty swallowing? REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT of the Chest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: High-Resolution CT of the Chest: Ground-glass opacities and reticular markings consistent with interstitial lung disease. No evidence of large pleural effusions or pneumothorax.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you ever worked in a job involving mining, construction, or shipyards where you might have been exposed to silica or asbestos? REQUEST TEST: Serum Silica and Asbestos Exposure Markers. Also, do you have a history of smoking, and have you noticed any clubbing of your fingers or toes?

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the normal exposure markers make occupational lung disease less likely. Given the restrictive pattern and ground-glass opacities, have you noticed any recent weight loss, night sweats, or a chronic cough producing blood? REQUEST TEST: Serum Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) and Soluble Interstitial Cell Adhesion Molecule-1 (sICAM-1).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; normal ACE and sICAM-1 levels make sarcoidosis and some forms of hypersensitivity pneumonitis less likely. Given the restrictive pattern and ground-glass opacities without a clear autoimmune or occupational cause, have you noticed any recent viral infections, and do you have a history of lung transplantation or significant radiation therapy?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any recent viral infections, and I've never had lung surgery or radiation treatment. I just feel like my lungs are getting tighter and harder to breathe with every day. However, hospital policy during the current surge is to avoid non-essential labs. Cardiac diagnosis must be made from clinical evaluation only.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF). Given the restrictive pattern, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, ground-glass opacities, and the absence of autoimmune, occupational, or infectious causes, this clinical picture is most consistent with IPF.
